source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Worksheet Step 1 lines 1-7, Step 2 lines 8-13 and instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1s; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 49,950.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 + interest 23,050.00 = 107,000.00. Federal taxable income = 107,000.00 - 23,625.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 81,375.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 107,000.00. Line 1s, Social Security worksheet: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70). Line 3 federal AGI 107,000.00; line 4 Head of household; line 5 born on or before 03/01/1959: yes; line 6 107,000.00; line 7 107,000.00 less than 107,000.00: no. STOP: not eligible; modification 0.00. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70): yes; question 2 federal AGI 107,000.00 less than or equal to 107,000.00: yes. Table: person 0 line 2 49,950.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 49,950.00; line 4 = 49,950.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 49,950.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 49,950.00 = -49,950.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -49,950.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 107,000.00 + (-49,950.00) = 57,050.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 57,050.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 16,350.00 (Head of household). Line 5 = 57,050.00 - 16,350.00 = 40,700.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 40,700.00 - 5,100.00 = 35,600.00. Line 8 tax on 35,600.00 by the schedule as numbers: 35,600.00 x 0.0375 = 1335.000000 = 1,335.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 1,335.00. Note: Head of household at exactly 107,000: the pension test keeps the relief, the Social Security test does not.
accepted_approximations: The pension test keeps the relief at exactly the limit, as instructions line 1t asks ('less than or equal to'); the statute printed in the Guide says 'less than'.
